concerns.text: T006 requires a chi-square test of exclusion vs. condition, but I/O-pair extraction (T006) runs on the original Python corpus BEFORE any condition is applied — exclusion is a property of the snippet alone, identical across all four conditions, so the contingency table is degenerate by construction and the test cannot produce a meaningful χ². The plan (Phase 3 task 5) has the same root flaw. Either define the conditioning variable differently (e.g., exclusion vs. dataset source) or drop the test; as written the task is not executable as specified.

T004 is too coarse: one task bundles run_inference.py, timeout_utils.py, retry/backoff logic, non-code detection, output hierarchy, and metadata logging (re-opening five rejected artifacts T009/T022/T023/T024/T025c). Split so each rejected artifact and its contract test is independently deliverable/verifiable; the atomizer will do this, but flagging to trigger it.

T009 is too coarse: it re-runs inference, extraction, validation, and quality (four prior tasks' outputs) plus checkpoint/fallback decision logic in one task. The mid-run checkpoint extrapolation and fallback-recording logic should be a separately verifiable unit (e.g., a checkpoint function with a unit test on a synthetic elapsed-time table).

T012's verification is 'Manual/automated review confirms every numeric claim traces to an existing CSV cell' — no named artifact or command. Name the mechanism, e.g. a script `code/src/evaluation/check_paper_traceability.py` that extracts numbers from methods_and_results.md and matches them against CSV cells, so done-ness is checkable.
T011's verification references 'A check script' without a path. Name it (e.g., `code/tests/contract/test_summary_table.py`) so the deliverable is concrete.

'Sandboxed subprocess' is unspecified (no isolation mechanism, resource limits, or working directory named). A plain subprocess with timeout satisfies the verification as written; either specify the sandbox mechanism or drop the word to avoid an unverifiable adjective.

T008 does not state how ESLint complexity is computed for syntactically invalid generated JS (failed translations produce no parse tree). Specify the fallback row value (e.g., complexity_score = 0 or a skipped status) so the CSV is well-defined for all files.
